Excel to Statistics

Fast tools that run in your browser. No login, no sign-up.

Everything runs in your browser. Your text and files are not uploaded to our servers. No account or login is needed.

How to use

  1. Upload an Excel or CSV file, paste cells copied from Excel, or type your data with column names in the first row. Load example data lets you try it first.
  2. Check the variable types, tick the analyses and charts you want, choose their variables and, for descriptive statistics, the exact statistics to show.
  3. Press Run analysis, then copy the tables or download them as an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file, and save each chart as SVG or PNG.

About this tool

Turn spreadsheet data into statistics and charts without writing code. Upload an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file, paste cells copied from Excel, or type the values by hand, then tick what you want: descriptive statistics (you choose exactly which ones, optionally by group), frequency tables, normality tests, homogeneity of variances, correlation, t-tests, one-way and two-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD, Mann–Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal–Wallis, Friedman, chi-square, binomial test, linear and logistic regression and Cronbach's alpha. Eight chart types are included: bar chart, histogram, box plot, scatter plot, line chart, pie chart, Q–Q plot and correlation heat map. Tables can be copied or downloaded as Excel or CSV, charts as SVG or PNG, and everything is calculated in your browser.

Frequently asked questions

Which files can I use, and what are the limits?

Files in .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, .tsv and .txt format, or cells pasted from Excel or Google Sheets. Old .xls and .ods files are not read: save the sheet as .xlsx or CSV first. Formulas are read as their last saved values, and date cells are treated as text categories. The limits are 100,000 rows, 200 columns and 15 MB.

Do the results match Excel and SPSS?

The standard definitions are used: quartiles by the inclusive method (the same as Excel QUARTILE.INC), variance and standard deviation with n − 1, skewness and kurtosis as in Excel SKEW and KURT, Student and Welch t-tests, Shapiro–Wilk, Tukey HSD, type III sums of squares for two-way ANOVA, exact Wilcoxon and Mann–Whitney p-values for small samples without ties, and Yates correction for 2×2 tables. Spearman p-values use the t approximation and Lilliefors p-values are approximate, so they can differ slightly from other programs in very small samples.

How are missing values handled?

Empty cells and the entries NA, N/A, #N/A, NaN, null and - count as missing. Each analysis uses the valid values of its own variables: pairs for correlations and paired tests, complete rows for regression and chi-square. The variable table shows the valid and missing counts, and text found in a numeric column is skipped and marked with ×.

How are decimal marks and number columns handled?

Choose automatic, dot or comma for typed or CSV data; automatic looks at the values and falls back to the language of the page. Thousands separators are accepted. Numbers inside an Excel file are always read exactly. A column is numeric only if every non-empty value is a number, so if a column shows as Category, check the decimal mark or change its type in the variable table. Columns coded 1, 2, 3 can still be used as grouping variables.

Which charts and tests are included?

Charts: bar chart (counts, percentages, means with error bars, clustered or stacked), histogram with an optional normal curve, box plot (also by group), scatter plot with trend line, line chart, pie chart, normal Q–Q plot and correlation heat map. Tests: descriptive statistics (also by group), frequencies, Shapiro–Wilk, Anderson–Darling, Lilliefors and Jarque–Bera normality tests, Levene and Bartlett, correlation, one-sample, independent and paired t-tests, one-way and two-way ANOVA, Mann–Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal–Wallis, Friedman, chi-square (independence and goodness of fit), Fisher, binomial test, linear and logistic regression, and Cronbach's alpha.

Is my data uploaded or stored?

No. The tool runs in your browser, so what you enter stays on your device and is not stored by us. The only exception is the standard server log kept by the hosting provider, described in the Privacy Policy.
